# Mahāsaṅgāma (Pvr 15)

**ID:** Pvr 15
**Section:** Parivāra (pvr)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Mahāsaṅgāma
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** The great chapter on the resolution of conflicts

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mahāsaṅgāma* ("The Great Chapter on the Resolution of Conflicts") is the fifteenth chapter of the *Parivāra*, the final collection of the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The text sets forth the rules, procedures, and requirements to be observed when a monastic addresses or speaks on matters of conflict (*adhikaraṇa*) before the Saṅgha [SuttaCentral]. As discussed in secondary monastic legal manuals, the chapter establishes that disputes may be adjudicated by a complete Saṅgha, an assembled group (*gaṇa*, such as an *ubbāhikā* committee), or a single senior individual (*puggala* / *saṅghathera*), depending on the gravity of the matter [Entrance to the Vinaya Vol. 3 1983].

Modern translations include an English translation by Bhikkhu Brahmali listed on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral]. Although SuttaCentral lists no direct curated parallels in other Buddhist canonical collections [SuttaCentral], computational analysis by DharmaNexus indicates extensive text reuse across the Pali Canon and Tibetan and Sanskrit corpora [DharmaNexus]. Internally, the *Mahāsaṅgāma* shares thousands of characters with Khandhaka and Parivāra treatises—chiefly the *Kosambakakkhandhaka* (Kd 10), *Upālipañcaka* (Pvr 17), *Saṁghabhedakakkhandhaka* (Kd 17), *Pavāraṇākkhandhaka* (Kd 4), *Samathakkhandhaka* (Kd 14), *Antarapeyyāla* (Pvr 4), and *Codanākaṇḍa* (Pvr 13)—as well as numerous numerical suttas in the Aṅguttara Nikāya (AN 1, AN 2, AN 4, AN 5, and AN 10) and Vinaya commentary/subcommentary literature such as the *Kaṅkhāvitaraṇīpurāṇa-ṭīkā* and *Vinayasaṅgaha-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Cross-linguistically, text segments are aligned by DharmaNexus with Sanskrit fragments of the *Pravāraṇāvastu*, as well as Tibetan translations of Vinaya treatises including the *Vinayavastu* (D 1), the *Yogācārabhūmau Vinayasaṃgrahaṇī* (D 4040), the *Saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtaviniścaya* (D 3897), the *Pratimokṣasūtraṭīkāvinayasamuccaya* (D 4106-2), and the *Vinayasūtraṭīkā* (D 4120) [DharmaNexus].
